newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN BUNDS TO BE HELD DOWN AHEAD OF U.S. DATA.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN BUNDS TO BE HELD DOWN AHEAD OF U.S. DATA.

text.p: German Bunds and futures will find little scope for a move to the upside ahead of key inflation releases from the U.S. on Wednesday.

A rally in the Bund market, prompted on Tuesday by a Bundesbank decision to leave the repo rate fixed at three percent, was all but wiped out at the open as the German market was undermined by Treasury weakness.
Traders said that this session too would see Bunds being led almost exclusively by the U.S. market.
"There isn't much chance of independent moves today in Bunds, especially with the U.S. fugures coming up," said one.
By 0726 GMT, the September DTB Bund future was down 30 basis points on the day at 101.94, but off its earlier low of 101.82.
Technical analysts said the 101.82/84 region should provide some support, with 101.75 coming in beyond there.

U.S. retail sales and producer price data for July are due at 1230 GMT, with debt markets awaiting the releases with a certain amount of nervousness after the report showing economic strength hit the Treasury market on Tuesday.
The Redbook report was up 0.9 pct in the first week of August with retailers saying sales were better than expected.

At the short end of the market, domestic rate concerns and currency movements will continue to hold sway, analysts said, after shorter-dated paper failed to find much comfort in the Bundesbank's steady hand on the repo on Tuesday.

The mark strengthened marginally after the Bundesbank report earlier in the session in which the bank said it could not be overlooked that there had been a stronger rise in consumer prices in recent months.
The Bundesbank also said it would orient its monetary policy to ensure price stability could be maintained.
The dollar was trading at 1.8540/50 by 0747 GMT.
But analysts said the boost to the mark, both from the repo decision on Tuesday and from the Bundesbank's inflation warning, was likely to be relatively short lived.
"Tuesday's attack of 1.8700 (on dollar/mark) will probably give way to a test of 1.9000 pretty soon," said Aufderheide.
